t: Core Principles of Fault-Tolerant Universal Quantum Computers
title: Core Principles of Fault-Tolerant Universal Quantum Computers
provenance: Public research knowledge: documented developments, published research, and established technical references. Real, fact-checked records.
description: Four principles govern fault-tolerant universal quantum computers. Principle 1: coherence is the currency: every design decision is judged by how well it preserves it. Principle 2: error correction turns fragile physics into reliable computing, at the cost of overhead. Principle 3: the compiler is part of the machine: software and hardware must be co-designed. Principle 4: claims require benchmarks: performance is proven on standard workloads, not asserted. The piece records show where each principle is enforced in hardware and software.

t: Key Vocabulary of Fault-Tolerant Universal Quantum Computers
title: Key Vocabulary of Fault-Tolerant Universal Quantum Computers
provenance: Public research knowledge: documented developments, published research, and established technical references. Real, fact-checked records.
description: Six terms unlock the whole database. qubit: the basic unit of quantum information, a controllable two-level quantum system. decoherence: loss of quantum behavior through unwanted interaction with the environment. error correction: encoding logical information across many physical units to survive faults. photonic processor: a chip that computes with light instead of (or alongside) electrons. neuromorphic: computing designed around brain-inspired, event-driven signaling. benchmark: a standard workload used to compare machines fairly. The glossary program below looks up any of these terms instantly; use it while reading the other records.
